title: InfoGeo: Information-Theoretic Object-Centric Learning for Cross-View Generalizable UAV Geo-Localization
claim: Prior methods keep view-specific noise in their features; ours isolates view-invariant object clues and so generalizes better across domains.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: annotated photo pair, token comparison, bar charts
description: A wide three-panel figure. Panel (a), Motivation, is the largest. It shows a satellite aerial image and a UAV aerial image of the same building. Green hatched boxes mark view-specific noise regions. A blue box on the satellite image and an orange box on the UAV image mark the view-invariant region. Red lines join orange circles that mark matched key visual clues in the two views. Panel (b), Overview, has a legend for tokens and noise. It contrasts Previous Methods, which pass noisy hatched tokens, with InfoGeo (Ours). In the InfoGeo path a green funnel labeled Noise Suppression, plus an OCL model robot icon, outputs clean view-invariant tokens. Panel (c), Comparison, has two grouped bar charts of R@1 and mAP for four methods. InfoGeo is the darkest, tallest bar, with red arrows marking gains of 3–5%.
caption: (a) The illustration of our motivation. Cross-view images can be decomposed into the view-invariant information and view-specific noise, while paired data can be matched through key visual clues. (b) The overview of cross-view object-centric learning process, the main target is to extract view-invariant tokens by compressing the view-specific noise. (c) Comparison with recent state-of-the-art methods on the two transfer scenarios, our method is built upon the model CVcities and achieves superior generalization ability.
abstract: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) is fundamental for precise localization and navigation in GPS-denied environments, aiming to match ground or UAV imagery with satellite views. Existing approaches often rely on global feature alignment, but they suffer from substantial domain shifts induced by varying regional textures and weather conditions. This issue becomes even more pronounced in UAV-based scenarios, where the broader perspective inevitably introduces dense, fine-grained objects, creating significant visual clutter. To address this, we draw inspiration from Object-Centric Learning (OCL) and propose InfoGeo, an information-theoretic framework designed to enhance robustness and generalization. InfoGeo reformulates the optimization as an information bottleneck process with two core objectives: (i) maximizing view-invariant information by aligning the object-centric structural relations across views, and (ii) minimizing view-specific noisy signals through cross-view knowledge constraints. Extensive evaluations across diverse benchmarks and challenging scenarios demonstrate that InfoGeo significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
